liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **El Paso** (1 review): Garcia slips in brilliant riffs after specific lyrics in the El Paso performance [14]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): The performance is considered the greatest tripped-out Dark Star ever played by the band [10]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): The end of Sugar Magnolia is cited as proof the show deserves a full release [10]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-10-31.142426.sbd.gans.eaton.miller.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 136 min; rated 4.57/5 by 7 [1]
- **gd1971-10-31.sbd.miller.79011.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 15 songs; 78 min; rated 4.75/5 by 12 [2]. Said about its sound: Keith's piano is crisp and present, unlike the official release where it is inaudible; The audio quality is described as being of Charlie Miller standard, which is sufficient; Instrument separation is better on this recording than on Dick's Picks Volume 2 [3][4][7][8][9][13]

## Around the show

- Jerry Garcia played steel guitar with the New Riders of the Purple Sage as an opening act [5]
- Pigpen was absent due to illness, and the venue was the newly renovated Ohio Theatre [5]
- Garcia asked the crowd to jump on the floor instead of seats between songs [5]
- Only four of the fifteen songs in set one come from the Skull and Roses album [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-10-31.142426.sbd.gans.eaton.miller.flac1644**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Master Reel (7in @ 7.5ips 1/2trk) > Dat (Panasonic SV-3700/44.1k) [1]. Also: Thanks are given to David Gans and Rob Eaton for the Dats; The first few notes of Bertha and Jack Straw are missing from the recording [1]
- **gd1971-10-31.sbd.miller.79011.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (44.1k) D [2]. Also: Charlie Miller's transfer is praised for doing the recording and concert justice; A reel flip in Tennessee Jed was fixed with a crossfade [2][3]
